body:

I hope you are doing well!! Here I'm again with my ideas :)

body:
Hi Aurelio,

Perfect! Thanks for keeping me updated.

Regarding your inquiry, the Screen State data source is supported on both iOS and Android, while the App Usage data source is only available on Android devices. In fact, Apple has a very strict policy and doesn't let third parties get this information.

The only viable approach to get this data objectively on iOS devices is by using Apple's SensorKit. However, it's worth mentioning that this method is time-consuming and consequently more expensive. We are required to submit a request to Apple, and it typically takes approximately 2 months for them to respond. Upon approval from Apple, we can create a custom app for your project and collect any data you want from iOS devices. You can find more details here. Please let me know if you would like to pursue this option, and we can discuss it further.

As for your other question, Bluetooth Beacons are supported on both Android and iOS without any user restrictions.

For further questions, please don't hesitate to contact me.

Best,
Sara

Hi Aurelio,

I confirmed with Amin and reviewed our session recording. During the meeting, Amin shared the same link from our Learn website with you and also provided this link to a project that uses Bluetooth Beacons.

I discussed the devices with the team, and they mentioned that as long as the beacon supports the iBeacon standard, it doesn’t matter which one you purchase. You can opt for a more affordable manufacturer, and it should work just fine.

To give you more insight, the price differences are due to several factors:
  1. Additional features offered by the beacon (for example, some include an accelerometer).
  2. Battery life (surprisingly, more features often result in shorter battery life).
  3. Brand and overall quality.
  4. Software quality for programming the beacon.

I hope this information helps you find a suitable device. If there’s anything else we can assist you with, please let us know.

Best,
Sara

On 25 Sep 2024, at 00:42, Sara Farnya <sales@avicennaresearch.com> wrote:

Hi Aurelio,
I confirmed with Amin and reviewed our session recording. During the meeting, Amin shared the same link from our Learn website with you and also provided this link to a project that uses Bluetooth Beacons.
I discussed the devices with the team, and they mentioned that as long as the beacon supports the iBeacon standard, it doesn’t matter which one you purchase. You can opt for a more affordable manufacturer, and it should work just fine.
To give you more insight, the price differences are due to several factors:
  1. Additional features offered by the beacon (for example, some include an accelerometer).
  2. Battery life (surprisingly, more features often result in shorter battery life).
  3. Brand and overall quality.
  4. Software quality for programming the beacon.
I hope this information helps you find a suitable device. If there’s anything else we can assist you with, please let us know.
Best,
Sara
